title: Infra consolidated: GPU fleet, capacity, IaC modules, CI/CD, and runbooks
author: Marcus Chen
summary: Consolidated playbook for infra engineers covering GPU fleet & capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking guidelines, Terraform/IaC module standards, CI/CD pipelines for infra, and primary runbooks used during incidents.
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates operational standards and runbook procedures for the infra organization focused on GPU fleet and capacity, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD pipelines. It is intended as the team wiki canonical reference for new hires, oncall engineers, and cross-team owners.

Scope:
- GPU fleet provisioning, autoscaling policy and capacity planning
- Network design for dedicated inference clusters (VPC/subnets, peering, shared services)
- Terraform module patterns, state management, and module registry guidance
- CI/CD best practices for infra repositories and promotion flows
- Runbooks for common alerts, incident escalation, and rollback procedures

Owner and contact: eng-infra (primary). Oncall rotation and escalation are maintained in the oncall schedule (see Team PagerDuty). For triage ownership: GPU Fleet -> @gpu-fleet; Cloud & Networking -> @cloud-net; IaC & CI -> @infra-platform.

1) GPU fleet and capacity planning

Goals and SLOs:
- Maintain 99.9% cluster availability for Dedicated pools during business hours (08:00–20:00 PT).
- Median cold-start latency for single-request inference <= 120ms on p4d-equivalent instances (for pinned models).
- Queueing latency SLA: 95th percentile request queue wait <= 250ms under steady-state.

Sizing guidance:
- Use historical QPS and per-request token median to estimate GPU-second demand. Example formula: required_gpu_hours/day = (avg_tokens_per_request * avg_requests_per_day * per_token_ms) / (3600 * gpu_fraction_utilization). Keep utilization target 60–75% to avoid tail latency spikes.
- Default instance families: p4d/p4de (large throughput), a10g/a100s for mixed workloads; use smaller a2/a10 for low-cost dev clusters.

Autoscaling policy (recommended):
1. Monitor two signals: queue_length(tokenized_requests) and GPU_utilization (avg over 1m).
2. Scale up when: queue_length > 4 * GPUs OR GPU_utilization > 70% for 2 consecutive 1m buckets.
3. Scale down when: queue_length == 0 AND GPU_utilization < 30% for 10 minutes.
4. Use step-scaling: +20% capacity on scale-up, -10% on scale-down.

Capacity safety margins and pre-warming:
- Maintain a 20% reserved buffer for business hours for latency-sensitive customers.
- Pre-warm nodes for large scheduled rollouts: create target capacity at least 15 minutes prior to canary traffic.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Node launch failures: auto-retry with exponential backoff; if > 3 consecutive failures within 10m, escalate to infra oncall and fallback to hosted variants by routing policy.
- Spot eviction impact: maintain mixed pools with 25% on-demand baseline for critical routes.

2) Cloud accounts and networking

Account structure and ownership:
- Use a 'landing-zone' account for shared services (bastions, artifact registries, central logging).
- Separate accounts for environments: prod-dedicated, prod-hosted, staging, dev. Account creation requires security review and ownership tag.
- Billing tags and cost centers required on all resources.

Network design patterns:
- VPC per account with segmented subnets: management (private-no-egress), inference (private-with-nat), public (ingress endpoints only).
- Use shared services VPC for central logging/metrics endpoints; connect via VPC peering or Transit Gateway depending on scale.
- Subnet sizing: reserve /22 for inference pools to allow IP churn during scale.

Connectivity and security controls:
- Ingress rules: only allow control plane traffic from Redwood control-plane ranges; model-serving endpoints bound behind ALB/NLB with mTLS for cross-account calls.
- Egress: all egress must pass through NAT gateways with egress filtering; sensitive traffic (KMS/HSM) uses VPC endpoints.
- Firewall rules: deny-by-default; allow minimal ports (SSH on jumpbox, 443 for services, 9100/9090 for exporter scraping within VPC).

Network observability:
- Enable VPC flow logs to central logging with 7-day hot retention and 90-day cold.
- Use central tracer (X-Ray/Jaeger) headers propagated by application code; ensure model-serving runtime emits span for request lifecycle.

3) Terraform / IaC modules and state management

Repo structure and module policy:
- Keep modules small and composable. Naming: tf-mod-<purpose> (e.g., tf-mod-gpu-instance-pool).
- Modules live in infra-modules mono-repo; environment overlays in infra-environments repo.
- Module API must include: inputs for owner_tag, environment, capacity_min, capacity_max, instance_type, region, and tags.

State backend and locking:
- Use remote state in S3 with DynamoDB locking (AWS). Backend standard snippet:

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "redwood-terraform-state"
    key    = "envs/${var.environment}/${path_relative_to_repo}.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
    dynamodb_table = "redwood-tf-locks"
  }
}
```

Module lifecycle and versioning:
- Follow semantic versioning for module releases. Tag module releases and update downstream with a dependency PR linking to CHANGELOG.
- Breaking changes: maintain major version migration guide in module README.

Security and secrets:
- Do not store secrets in state. Use SSM Parameter Store / Secrets Manager; inject at runtime via CI secrets.
- Ensure IAM principals for state access are limited to terraform pipeline role and named humans (admin list).

4) CI/CD and build for infra repos

Pipeline patterns:
- PR checks: terraform fmt, tflint, checkov (policy-as-code), and terragrunt/terraform plan. Plan output must include a human-readable summary.
- Pipeline stages: validate -> plan (approved) -> apply (requires manual approval for prod branches).
- Apply runs under a short-lived deploy role assumed by pipeline; all actions must be logged to central audit.

Promotion strategy:
1. Merge to main triggers plan against staging env.
2. After smoke tests and canary validations, create a release PR to prod overlay.
3. Prod apply requires two approvers for modules modifying networking, KMS, or node pools.

CI best practices:
- Use ephemeral build agents with pre-warmed plugin cache.
- Artifacts: publish module package and lockfile SHA to artifact registry for reproducible builds.
- Automated drift detection: scheduled daily plan for prod to detect unexpected changes; create incidents on non-authorized drift.

Sample pipeline YAML (abridged):

```yaml
# .ci/terraform-pipeline.yaml
stages:
  - name: validate
  - name: plan
  - name: apply
steps:
  - validate: run: terraform init && terraform fmt -check && tflint
  - plan: run: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json
  - apply: when: manual; run: terraform apply tfplan; requires_approvals: 2
```

5) Runbooks and operational playbooks

On-call playbook (top-level):
- If alert: GPU pool under-provisioned (alert name: gpu.pool.capacity.low)
  1. Confirm alert: check dashboard panel for queue_length and GPU_utilization.
  2. Attempt automated scale: run infractl pool scale --pool $POOL --add 2
  3. If automation fails: check last 20 events in ASG/Autoscaler, verify quota in cloud account, then escalate to infra lead.
  4. If capacity cannot be restored in 10m: activate traffic routing policy to fallback model variant and notify product owners.

Deployment failure runbook (node bootstrap failing):
1. Check instance console output and cloud-init logs.
2. Roll a single failing node out of rotation: cordon -> drain -> terminate -> verify new node joins healthy.
3. If new node fails to bootstrap: capture logs, escalate to SRE and the runtime team with links to logs and instance id.

Incident playbook (network outage impacting inference):
- Triage: isolate whether outage is control-plane (API) or data-plane (NAT, route table).
- Mitigate: switch routing to an alternative AZ/TGW path; use pre-approved runbook to re-point ALB target groups to healthy pools.
- Post-incident: run RCA and update this document with timeline and change to scaling thresholds if necessary.

6) Runbook templates and checklists

Include: pre-deploy checklist, canary rollout steps, rollback criteria, post-deploy validation queries (sample PromQL queries included).

Sample Prometheus queries (validation):
- GPU_utilization_95p: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_utilization_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Request_queue_seconds_p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_queue_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

7) Team wiki and knowledge sharing

Docs to keep updated: module READMEs, deployment runbooks, incident timelines, capacity forecasts (quarterly). Every major change to autoscaling, instance types, or network design must have an ADR and an entry in the change-management template.

Onboarding checklist for new infra engineers:
- Read: this consolidated playbook, infra-modules README, GPU capacity runbook.
- Hands-on: create a non-prod overlay PR to add a tag and run pipeline.
- Shadow: 2 oncall shifts with senior engineer.

8) Change management and approvals

- Network & security-affecting changes require Security review and at least one network reviewer.
- Module breaking changes require an explicit migration plan and an announcement 2 weeks prior to release.

9) Related artifacts and references

- GPU capacity runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026.json
- IaC and GPU fleet guide: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026.json
- Infra team playbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/team-wiki/infra-engineering-playbook-2026.json

10) Maintenance and cadence

- Quarterly capacity review with product and SRE teams to update instance sizing and reserved buffers.
- Security & compliance review on all IaC changes quarterly for production accounts.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets

- Check ASG events: aws autoscaling describe-scaling-activities --auto-scaling-group-name $ASG_NAME --max-items 10
- Terraform plan against prod overlay (local dev): TF_VAR_environment=prod terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars
